status: frozen; to run on the SE-INR server after the ICME submission (needs the footprint stage-01 checkpoints and evaluation pipeline)
question: The footprint study proved that under symmetric training (c_x = c_y) the per-axis cell response of token-style decoders is not identified: for any layer that reads the cell linearly, only the sum of the two cell columns is constrained by the data. The input-side repair (feeding the geometric mean of c_x and c_y to both inputs) recovered 1.33 dB on LTE at asymmetric scales. Is the corresponding WEIGHT-side repair -- replace the two cell columns by their mean -- (a) an exact no-op on the training manifold, (b) as good as the input-side repair off it, and (c) findable from the weights alone?

edit.lte: phase.weight (hidden/2 x 2, no bias): W[:, 0] = W[:, 1] = (W[:, 0] + W[:, 1]) / 2. The phase then equals (W0 + W1) (c_x + c_y) / 2: the arithmetic-mean cell policy, written into 2 x hidden/2 weights.
edit.liif: imnet.layers.0.weight columns for the last two inputs (the attached cell): same averaging.
edit.sc-inr / sc-inr-exact: no edit: the cell enters through the analytic sinc, which is identified by construction.
edit.property: At c_x = c_y the edited network computes exactly what the original computed, because W0 c + W1 c = (W0 + W1) c. The repair cannot change any symmetric-scale number; this is checked numerically, not assumed.
edit.script: studies/05-assr-decoder/assr_symmetrize.py <checkpoint> <out> (reports the tensors and the count of changed entries)

evaluation: studies/footprint/01-inference run.py of the SE-INR footprint branch on the edited checkpoints, same conditions as stage 01 (symmetric 1.5-12, the 24 asymmetric pairs, downscale 0.5), three seeds, PSNR-Y with the stage-01 shave; paired per-image differences against the unedited checkpoints and against the input-side geometric-mean policy.

predictions_frozen_before_running.A1_noop_on_manifold: On every symmetric scale and every image, |PSNR(edited) - PSNR(original)| < 1e-4 dB for LTE and LIIF (floating-point only).
predictions_frozen_before_running.A2_lte_gain: On the asymmetric pairs, LTE edited minus original balanced PSNR-Y is at least +1.0 dB with the paired 95% interval above +0.7 dB, on each of the three seeds.
predictions_frozen_before_running.A3_arithmetic_vs_geometric: The weight-side (arithmetic-mean) repair is within 0.15 dB of the input-side geometric-mean repair on the asymmetric pairs; prior: slightly below it at the most asymmetric pairs (ratio 4 and 0.25), because (c_x + c_y)/2 > sqrt(c_x c_y) biases the phase towards the coarser axis.
predictions_frozen_before_running.A4_liif_small: LIIF edited minus original is within [-0.05, +0.10] dB on the asymmetric pairs (stage 01 found LIIF insensitive to cell swapping, -0.002 dB).
predictions_frozen_before_running.A5_seed_variance: The seed-to-seed range of LTE at asymmetric pairs drops from 0.9-3.6 dB to below 0.5 dB after the edit (the unidentified direction is what varied with the seed).

optional_llm_node: Give a frontier model the LTE decoder weights, the architecture, the training recipe (symmetric cells only) and the symptom (seed swings at asymmetric scales) under the sandbox protocol, and ask for a minimal repair. Scored by whether the submitted edit is the column average (or any edit that passes A1 and A2). Budget and model to be decided when the stage runs.
what_the_user_runs: On the server: python studies/05-assr-decoder/assr_symmetrize.py <epoch-last.pth> <edited.pth> for each LTE and LIIF seed; then the stage-01 freeze -> run -> score pipeline with --checkpoints pointing at the edited files; return score/summary.json and the per-image CSVs.
